videos.title: PvZ: Dark Templar Into Skytoss
videos.description:
Can Dark Templar buy you the time to get into Skytoss?

The idea is to use DTs to protect the third while two Void Rays pick off Overseers. If Zerg's push has no anti-air, meet it out on the map. That gives the Void Rays time to remove detection before the army reaches your Nexus.

From there, I go into a Mothership, Carriers and Archons. The tradeoff is how much tech you're buying with very few units on the map. If Zerg drones hard and gets fast Lair tech, this opening gets a lot less comfortable. I go through the scouting, the defenses and the decisions in this replay.

videos.title: PvZ, Can You Play It Without A Wall At The Start?
videos.description:
Can you open PvZ on the high ground and still take your natural? On four-player Fear and Faith LE, I walk through the opening and the decisions that come with delaying the wall.

The first Pylon, Gateway and Cybernetics Core go on the high ground. My recommendation is a Nexus at 17 supply, with the second Pylon on the low ground positioned for a later three-Gateway wall.

We cover the first Stalker against an Overlord, scouting with a hallucinated Phoenix, and the Nydus scout that changes when I move out. Then we look at a second replay where early Zerglings catch me off guard: Zealot + Probes to hold, a second Nexus already started, and an Adept as the priority.

The second-half scouting table corrects my original probability estimate. With three equally likely enemy spawns, a 50/50 Overlord route from the checked spawn, and a timely scout, no sighting gives 20% for that spawn and 40% for each of the other two—80% combined. This assumes only the checked spawn can send its Overlord past that scouting spot. Different routes or missed vision change those odds.

These are two replay examples, not a build win-rate test. You still need to respond to early pressure and build your wall later.

videos.title: PvT Stargate into Charge!
videos.description:
Terran is bringing Marines and tanks. Your Charge is nearly done. Do you wait—or fight before the bunkers finish?

In this PvT replay, I walk through Stargate into Charge: using Phoenix scouting to read the follow-up, keeping Zealots in production, and finding the moment to break the push.

The biggest things to watch:
• Double gas changes the plan: earlier units, defensive Chrono Boosts, and batteries.
• Keep scouting. Don’t assume Terran has expanded.
• Against this Marine–Tank push, prioritize Charge and keep the Gateways producing.
• Finish Charge, get another round of Zealots, and fight before the bunkers finish.
• After the hold, check what Terran has left. You don’t have to force the counterattack.

This is one of my own replay examples using the eight-worker setup discussed in the video. I also point out the late battery and scouting risks so you can see where the execution needs work.

videos.description:
This Zerg scouted my Glaives. Keeping the Adepts alive let me continue the pressure and take his third anyway.

In this StarCraft II PvZ replay guide, I walk through a Core-first Adept opener using an eight-worker setup: early two-Adept pressure, the three-Gateway Glaive follow-up, and the decision to preserve the army when the defense is ready. From there, we add Gateways and Stalkers, pressure the third near the edge of creep, and expand behind the attack.

The intended upgrade after Glaives is Blink. I accidentally queue Charge in this game, so I explain the mistake and how I adapt before moving into Blink and Immortals. Copy the intended build, and use the replay to understand the decisions when execution gets messy.

The first player I personally saw use a version of this opener was Maplez, also known as Mape the Ape. Credit for that inspiration:

videos.title: 3 Rax, 1 Answer
videos.description:
I’ve been seeing more 3 Rax in my Protoss vs Terran games on StarCraft II’s 8-worker patch. My answer is one Protoss unit type: the Sentry.

That does not mean making literally one Sentry. When I’m not playing Blink, I go Sentry-heavy: scout the Barracks count, use Guardian Shield against the bio, shape the fight with Force Fields, and make the Terran engage before Medivacs and Tanks take over.

These two Grandmaster ladder games show two ways to use the same idea.

STANDARD OPENER
14 Gateway → 17 Nexus → 17 Gas → 17 Cybernetics Core

GAME 1 — ROBO / COLOSSUS VERSION
A Hallucinated Phoenix confirms the opening after the Zealot scout is denied. Because my Robo is already started, I keep it: Observer, Immortals, Robo Bay, five Gateways, then a one-Colossus timing. The Observer tracks the army, and the push lands as the first two Medivacs arrive.

GAME 2 — FASTER NO-ROBO VERSION
The Zealot sees the three Barracks immediately, so I skip the Robo and reach the five-Gate pressure faster with roughly six to eight Sentries. A small warp-in handles the Marine backstab while the main army keeps pressing.

THE FOUR RULES
• Get the Sentry early enough to scout—or recharge it for the scout
• If you are not opening Blink, be Sentry-heavy
• Keep the Terran army in front so your Force Fields stay strong
• Move before Medivacs and Tanks are established, and watch for the backstab

This is not one rigid build order. It is a way to read 3 Rax and choose the right branch from the position you already have.

videos.title: PvT 1 Unit DT Drop?
videos.description:
Can you reach a fast DT drop in PvT while defending with only ONE early combat unit?

The “1 Unit” is the setup: one Stalker holds the wall while Protoss techs through Twilight Council, Robotics Facility, and Dark Shrine. The actual Warp Prism attack uses THREE Dark Templars, split across both Terran mineral lines.

This is my 8-worker-patch update of the old PiLiPiLi 12-worker version. The opening is 17 Nexus / 17 Gas / 17 Core, but the key is the scout: if Terran shows two gas, do not force the greedy version—add units and batteries or change the plan.

What makes the build work:
• One chronoed Stalker denies the Reaper and does double duty
• Robo + two Gateways + a Shield Battery complete the wall
• Twilight → Robo → Dark Shrine keeps the real threat hidden
• A chronoed Warp Prism routes around the army and approaches the main
• Three DTs split the mineral lines while three Stalkers stop the counterattack

The Prism gets sniped, but Terran has two Command Centers and zero scans. That is all the DTs need.

videos.title: PvZ Stargate into Glaive Adept Timing
videos.description:
This PvZ build hides an 18-Glaive-Adept timing behind what looks like a normal Stargate opener—and punishes Zerg players who drone too hard.

I open with two Adepts for scouting and split pressure, spend 150 gas on the Stargate, and lead with a Void Ray to clear Overlords and hide the follow-up. Behind it: a third Nexus, four total Gateways, a Twilight Council, and one final Adept round that takes the army from 14 to 18.

The key is to move before Resonating Glaives finishes, so the upgrade completes as the Adepts reach the Zerg bases.

In this game, the Zerg reaches 77 drones. The split shades force two bases to be defended at once—and the greed gets punished.

This is a ladder tool, not a guaranteed win. The opening also includes a more expensive double scout because this is a four-player map, so adjust it to your map and what you see.

BUILD CHECKLIST
• 14 Gateway / 17 Nexus on this four-player map
• Two Adepts for early scouting and pressure
• Stargate at 150 gas
• Void Ray first to disguise the follow-up
• Third Nexus → two more Gateways + Twilight Council
• Clear nearby Overlords before revealing Glaives
• Produce Adepts from four Gateways
• Move before Glaives completes
• Add the final round: 14 → 18 Adepts
• Choose Fleet Beacon, Blink + Forge, or Robo based on the scout

videos.title: PvP Proxy 1 Gate?
videos.description:
StarCraft II Protoss vs Protoss (PvP) analysis on Patch 5.0.16b: can a one-Gateway proxy really work in the new 8-worker meta?

I break down the proxy location, Probe timing, Chrono plan, scouting information, first two Zealots, Adept follow-up, double-tech transition, and the one defensive reaction that decides the entire game.

The key moment is brutally small: the opponent's Pylon block is a fraction of a second late. The Adept gets in, the opponent falls to 15 Probes, and the lead reaches +8 workers at four minutes. From there, the build transitions into two Immortals, a Warp Prism, Glaive Adepts, and nonstop pressure.

QUICK BUILD NOTES
• Send one of your first 8 Probes across the map
• Proxy a single Gateway; keep the second Pylon at home
• Add both Assimilators and keep Probe production running
• Save Chrono Boost for the first two Zealots
• Scout when the proxy Gateway is about 75% complete
• Start the Cybernetics Core at home and protect the ramp with a hard wall
• Follow with Adepts while adding Robotics Facility + Stargate
• Build two Immortals, then a Warp Prism
• Add Twilight Council, Glaives, and more Gateways for the timing attack

DEFENDING THIS BUILD
Hard-wall the ramp before the first Zealot arrives. The replay shows exactly why being one second late can turn a manageable proxy into a game-ending worker deficit.

videos.title: PvZ Cracking 8 Pools
videos.description:
The 8 Pool is the fastest Zergling rush in StarCraft II—but this 13-Gateway PvZ response turns it into a 10-worker lead. This Protoss vs. Zerg guide shows the complete defense: scout it, wall it, hold it, then punish it with four Adepts.

▬▬▬▬▬ THE 8-POOL RESPONSE ▬▬▬▬▬

• 13 Gateway, then scout immediately with the Gateway Probe
• No natural? Enter the main and confirm the early Spawning Pool
• Add a second Gateway, Cybernetics Core, and Assimilator ASAP
• Chrono Boost the first Zealot and stop at 19 Probes
• Pre-build Pylons—without a Nexus, the supply block arrives fast
• At the wall: poke, retreat, and never give the Zerglings a surround
• Let the first Adepts finish the hold, then make four total
• Start the Nexus once 16 Probes are mining minerals
• Counterpressure with the Adepts; Recall if mass Lings are waiting
• If Zerg drones, punish the mineral line

The payoff in this game: a clean hold, a 10-worker lead, and the freedom to follow with Stargate, Twilight Council, or the Robo setup from the previous PvZ guide.

videos.title: I Tried AlphaStar's PvP Build on the 8-Worker Build... It Shouldn't Work
videos.description:
AlphaStar's AI created the original version of this wild Protoss vs Protoss build. I adapted the same idea to the modern 8-worker patch: fast Adept pressure, an Oracle split, then an unusual two-Immortal timing that turns one greedy third base into a losing position.

The replay is not perfect — the 12 Pylon is late — which makes the result more useful: you can see the recovery, the scouting branches, and why the build still works without robotic execution. The attack finishes 20 supply ahead and takes the win.

FULL BUILD ORDER
• 12 Pylon (the replay is late; recover without panicking)
• Double gas, second Gateway, then Cybernetics Core
• Second Pylon → scout
• Use 3 Chrono Boosts on the Nexus for Probe production
• 2 Adepts + Warp Gate
• Stargate, then 2 more Adepts
• Oracle first; threaten the natural with Adepts and the main with the Oracle
• Add the Nexus, then Robotics Facility
• Chrono 2 Immortals back-to-back
• Add Gateways to reach 5–6 total
• When the third appears, swap to Warp Gates and move out
• Hallucinate 1 Immortal to obscure the real targets
• Pressure the third while the Oracles hit the main
• Transition to Blink and a third Nexus while keeping the opponent pinned

IMPORTANT SCOUTING BRANCH
If the first scout sees two early Stalkers, do not blindly make four Adepts. Add a Shield Battery and make defensive Stalkers; the Adept version is vulnerable to concentrated Stalker pressure.

videos.title: The PvT Build With The Highest Floor In StarCraft II (Grandmaster Protoss Guide)
videos.description:
Full Grandmaster PvT build order breakdown — 12 Pylon, 14 Gateway into a 17 Nexus,
three Gateways off one base, and a Stalker attack that hits the front and the main at
the same time. Very high floor, easy to execute, and the only real skill check is your
probe micro against the Reaper.

FULL BUILD ORDER
12  Pylon
14  Gateway
14  Scout probe — cross-spawn on 4-player maps
17  Nexus (cutting probes)
17  Gas
17  Cybernetics Core
    Resume probe production
    Chrono the first Stalker — it has to beat the Reaper
    Warp Gate, chrono after the Stalker is out
    Proxy Pylon in the map tunnels (4-player maps only)
    Second Gateway, then a third — 3-Gate off one base
    Warp in 3 Stalkers, hit the front and the main together
    Deny the expansion — that is the win condition
    Transition: Twilight Council, third Nexus, then Robotics

WHY THIS BUILD
It is safe against the Reaper opening, it does not need perfect execution, and it
punishes any Terran who commits to a fast expansion. A 16-16-16 opening gets a Stalker
out before the Reaper arrives — 17 Nexus does not, so you micro your probes for about
five seconds and you are fine.

videos.title: PvZ 3 Colossus 8 Gate Push: The PvZ Build That Wins Without Perfect Micro
videos.description:
Everyone says PvZ is unwinnable right now. It isn't — it's just hard, and you have to cut the right corners. This is the 17 Nexus into 3 Colossus 8-Gate push I use on the NA ladder as a Rank 21 Grandmaster Protoss, explained step by step from a full replay.

The whole build has a very high floor. There's no Stargate micro, no Disruptor shots to
land, no perfect Blink stalker dance. Nearly all of the skill expression is in one place:
the force fields you hit when the push arrives. Hit them, and the game usually ends there.

▬▬▬▬▬ THE FULL BUILD ORDER ▬▬▬▬▬

13  Gateway  (worse economy, but 8-pool becomes survivable)
13  Scout probe
17  Nexus — BEFORE gas
19  Cybernetics Core
20  Second gas, 3 workers on immediately
    2nd Pylon between the main and the natural
    Stalker first, no chrono
    Warp Gate
    Robotics Facility (robo first)
    Pylons on the base edges — anti-Nydus
    Sentry — scouts, then kills the overlord on the pillar
    2nd Gateway + Shield Battery
    Robotics Bay
    Immortal + expansion gases
    2nd Sentry
    Colossus x3 — chrono the robo NON-STOP
    Gateways up to 8 off two bases
45  Probes — 16 + 16 + one spare for proxy pylons
    Observer, then move out

Target: three Colossus by roughly the 7:00 mark, then push with force fields and warp
reinforcements into forward pylons.

▬▬▬▬▬ THINGS MOST PEOPLE GET WRONG ▬▬▬▬▬

13 Gateway is economically worse and I still do it. Below Masters, surviving pool-first
  is worth more than the mineral difference.
Everyone blocks the hatchery right now. This build doesn't need to.
17 Nexus before gas delays your tech by seconds and buys you a lot of minerals. In the
  current PvZ you have to be greedy somewhere.
Second pylon placement is a mind game, not a habit. Between main and natural forces the
  overlord deep, and Zerg hates losing overlords.
Randomise your first unit. An occasional Stalker-first out of a Stargate-looking opening
  means they might skip the Spore.
45 probes, not 44. The extra probe walks out with the army for proxy pylons.
See a fast Lair? Get more Stalkers immediately — 12 to 14 Mutas will end you otherwise.
